Saturn Vue service illustrations: applicability and visual limits

Reviewed 2026-10-14. The exact-part visual evidence for GM pan 12601240 is the official GM product imagery already retained in oil-pan-evidence/. The Saturn Vue service illustrations below are useful visual context, but they do not establish that the depicted pan is 12601240, and none supplies metric internal geometry.

Exact-part visual evidence

GM's 12601240 product page identifies the part and publishes its outside envelope (474.7 × 316 × 117.99 mm), 15 mounting holes, pickup inclusion and baffled description. The retained Primary photo shows the exterior; Alternate1 is an interior oblique photo showing the baffle and pickup routing. These official photos support qualitative topology for the named part, but do not provide internal dimensions, hole coordinates, datum locations or a calibrated view.

Vue illustration applicability

The retained source files and their byte counts and SHA-256 hashes are listed in pan-family-illustrations/manifest.json. Their classifications are:

FigureSource contextApplicabilityAllowed use
18680822008 Vue oil-pan cleaning and inspectionThe page shows pan-interior inspection callouts, but names neither engine nor pan part number.Unscaled, application-unresolved inspection illustration; visual context only.
1318093Same 2008 Vue cleaning and inspection pageBaffle-scraper inspection figure; the page names neither engine nor pan part number.Unscaled, application-unresolved component illustration; visual context only.
18667842008 Vue disassembled views, Figure 12The page itself does not name an engine. Its assembly callouts 405, 406, 410–413, 420 and 422 match the 2008 catalog entry for LY7 pan 12666374. The same figure is used in the 2009 Vue LY7/LCS manual context.Treat as an unscaled LY7 / 12666374 V6 analog, not as 12601240 evidence.

The 2008 Vue catalog lists 12601240 for LE5/LAT and 12666374 for LY7. It lists baffle 12578196 as part of an oil-pan assembly, while the 12666374 entry's callout set matches figure 1866784. Thus the catalog's presence of 12601240 and baffle 12578196 does not make the service illustrations same-part views. The Solstice LNF catalog independently identifies 12601240 and 12578196 for the target parts family; that identity does not identify which pan is shown in an unassigned Vue service procedure.

Modeling consequences

  • Use the official GM 12601240 interior photo for qualitative exact-part topology; do not derive dimensions from its perspective image.
  • Use Vue figures 1868082 and 1318093 only as application-unresolved illustrations. Use 1866784 only as a different-engine pan architecture analog.
  • Do not scale the Vue drawings, estimate boss coordinates from pixels or transfer Vue orientation to the Kappa chassis.
  • Keep cavity, cover, pickup path, floor, ribs, seats and placement as labeled proxy geometry. No metric geometry or CAD solids changed from this source correction.

Related digital path finding

The current model checks sampled vertical withdrawal with the cover removed, both with the pickup/tube proxy retained and with that complete proxy assembly absent. In the nominal proxy, A/B/C collide with the rising tube after 7 mm of lift; the proxy-only vertical path clears when the pickup/tube assembly is omitted. This is a digital assembly-sequence hypothesis, not a verified Solstice service instruction. See the scenario assessment for every context and the exact tested limits.
